title: FX revaluation posting blocks multi-currency checkout

verification.methodology: pact business verification (database + checkout SLO + protected ops)

checks.name: database_clear
checks.detail: No lock waits: no session is blocked.

audit.report: The ledger_fx_revaluation_post settlement job (PROTECTED_SETTLEMENT, never_interrupt) held an idle-in-transaction lock for 4.2s, blocking checkout sessions and degrading multi-currency checkout to 71-90% success vs 95% SLO with $3,286-$5,257/min revenue at risk. The Database Guardian investigated and found the job was non-replayable with ~36s expected remaining runtime; waiting would cost ~$3,137 but fit within the 60s degradation tolerance, while terminating would violate the never_interrupt policy and risk financial data integrity. Both guardians agreed to wait. The blocker finished immediately (0s waited) and checkout recovered to 100% success within 10s. The business is verified recovered: database clear, checkout SLO met, protected operations intact.
audit.root_cause: The ledger_fx_revaluation_post settlement job entered an idle-in-transaction state (last statement SELECT 1) for 4.2s, holding locks that blocked multi-currency checkout sessions and degraded success below SLO.
lessons: The ledger_fx_revaluation_post job (PROTECTED_SETTLEMENT, never_interrupt) can block checkout when idle in transaction — add a lock_timeout or statement_timeout for this workload to prevent indefinite blocking.

The blocker finished in 0s after the wait decision despite 4.2s idle — investigate why ledger_fx_revaluation_post enters idle-in-transaction state and whether the 40s typical runtime includes avoidable idle periods.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian initially proposed escalate but self-corrected to wait within R1 after gathering evidence on the workload's PROTECTED_SETTLEMENT class, never_interrupt policy, non-replayable nature, and trade-off analysis showing waiting fit within tolerance. The Continuity Guardian accepted without objection; no rounds were wasted and invariants (I1: never_interrupt + PROTECTED_SETTLEMENT) were respected.
follow_ups: Investigate why ledger_fx_revaluation_post enters idle-in-transaction state (last statement SELECT 1) and whether application logic can avoid holding locks while idle.
Add a lock_timeout or statement_timeout for the ledger_fx_revaluation_post job to prevent future checkout blocking.
Document the cost-per-second of checkout degradation ($3,286-$5,257/min) for this workload in the runbook to speed future trade-off decisions.
